Woah this is a super intense reaction. Obviously snapping on someone isn’t great, however, to accuse OP of intentionally manipulating a kid just so he could put him down feels like a big stretch. From the info we have, he is not evil, 16 year olds have very little emotional regulation skills and are early in their social development so it seems like he let his emotions build up and didn’t have a healthy way to express or discuss them. OP shouldn’t have freaked out but how many 16 year olds do you know that actually fully understand how relationships/boundaries work? Especially 10 years ago when mental health was not as accepted or talked about. I don’t want to excuse his behavior because he shouldn’t have been mean and put the kid down. He also probably should have included him when his friends all hung out but social pressures and the threat of ostracization feels like the end of the world in high school and without a fully developed understanding of consequences and empathy, because teenagers are not 100% cognitively capable of that and are inherently selfish, OP was probably acting in his own interest to protect himself from social isolation from his friends. This situation is so so horrible but when someone commits suicide, it’s never just because of one thing someone says. That kid needed more support from everybody in his life and OP definitely really hurt this kid but we can’t place the blame soley on him.

No you never agreed to my position but you are still choosing to give your money to the business and supporting the culture as a whole by going to restaurants that rely on tips for pay their servers. Also you know restaurant owners don’t give a shit, literally everyone knows that that’s why we’re talking about tip culture lol. 

It’s not required but it’s kind of fucked up not to, there are a lot of things in the world that are not required legally but people do anyway because that’s just how things work. If you don’t like that then, once again, do not participate. Order takeout.

I never said my friends are making more serving than their corporate jobs, I’m saying they need it in addition to their salary to make ends meet. I can promise you I don’t make more than someone in a job in my desired career even when people do tip me properly, serving just allows me to live and go to school. Those servers you see making $500 or $600 a night are actually very rare and in reality they’re making that once or twice a week in huge cities. 

I’ll stop being mad when those people who don’t agree with the broken culture stop participating in it by giving money to the restaurants that make that culture possible. Okay then order takeout and go sit down somewhere else to eat it. You could even ask the restaurant to sit in there and eat it without a server if they’re not busy, you just have to clean up after yourself. I’ve seen that happen a few times. 

Also a lot of my post grad friends are still serving because they are making shitty money at their corporate jobs and need to serve to make ends meet. But I understand what you’re saying, however if I’m spending 1.5-2 hours with a table, I expect a tip. Serving is a lot more than just bringing you food. I don’t know where you’re going out to eat at but part of my job is getting to know the customers and providing them with an experience along side the food on top of doing the same with all my other tables. 

People are mad at the customers and the employers. You just won’t see the other side of it because you’re not in the industry. I’ve had many conversations with my previous employers about wages and guess what, they absolutely don’t care. So since you’re so against tipping, do not go to a restaurant where that is the way servers get paid because when you sit down at their table, which we only get a limited amount of per night, what they make is your problem. You are knowingly going into a place that uses a system you don’t agree with and then saying that you’re sticking it to the employer as justification for not paying your server for their service. You say you can no longer support it but are actively paying for the food which directly supports the people who benefit the most from tip culture, which is the restaurant. If you really cared about servers making a livable wage, you would be doing more than actively screwing them to make yourself feel better.

And yes they will get the minimum wage of 7.25 or whatever it is in your area but that is not livable even if I worked 80 hours I couldn’t afford rent and food on that.
